outcome: Help relationship managers and digital channels recommend the most relevant eligible product or service at the right moment, with consent, suitability, and explainability controls.
overview: Banks and insurers hold rich customer data yet still run broad campaigns that convert poorly, fatigue customers and create conduct risk, while relationship managers search several systems to establish need and eligibility. This solution builds a permissioned customer view, detects approved life-event and service signals, applies consent, eligibility, suitability and affordability rules, then ranks a next-best action with the reasons behind it across assisted and digital channels — including recommending service recovery, education or no contact at all. A six to ten week proof of value tests one segment and product family against a randomised holdout, targeting higher conversion, better manager productivity, less campaign waste and more consistent customer treatment.

benefits.text: Increase conversion on eligible offers by a target 10–20% in the tested segment
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target range to validate against a randomised holdout in the customer’s own base — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Cut relationship-manager preparation time by a target 30% with a single permissioned customer summary
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on CRM adoption and on how many source systems the manager still has to open

benefits.text: Reduce irrelevant contact and campaign waste by suppressing offers that fail consent, eligibility or frequency rules
benefits.source: Reference design — policy gates run before ranking, per Redington BFSI catalogue
benefits.limits: Suppression quality is bounded by the accuracy of the customer’s consent and eligibility data

benefits.text: Give every recommendation a reason code and a policy trail that conduct and audit reviewers can inspect
benefits.source: Reference design — decision logging and fairness monitoring, Redington BFSI catalogue
benefits.limits: Explains which rules and signals drove the ranking; it does not replace the customer’s own suitability assessment

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); customer, consent and decision data stay inside the customer tenancy in both reference builds

notFor.situation: Consent and marketing-preference data is unreliable or not queryable at decision time
notFor.why: Every recommendation is gated on live consent and contact frequency; a stale preference store turns the engine into a compliance exposure rather than a growth tool

notFor.situation: Product eligibility and suitability rules exist only as written policy, not in machine-readable form
notFor.why: The decision layer can only enforce rules it can evaluate; hand-interpreted policy cannot be applied consistently or evidenced

notFor.situation: No holdout or control group is permitted, so incremental lift cannot be attributed
notFor.why: Conversion moves for many reasons; without a control the benefit case is a correlation, and the PoV cannot honestly be judged

notFor.situation: Recommendations would be sent with no human review on adverse or high-impact actions
notFor.why: Conduct risk in regulated markets requires an accountable human on suitability-sensitive offers

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns product, conduct, consent and all customer communication · Duration: 6–10 weeks to proof of value; a further 14–24 weeks to production omnichannel decisioning
Delivery pod: Partner project lead + technical lead, vendor platform specialist, data scientist; customer revenue sponsor, product owner, CRM and channel owner, data owner, conduct and privacy reviewers, model-risk reviewer, finance analyst and pilot relationship managers · Support model: Business-hours standard with an extended-hours option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation; optional managed optimisation
1) Discovery and growth-baseline agreement
2) Segment, rule and control-group design
3) Permissioned customer-data build
4) Model and decision configuration
5) CRM and channel integration
6) Fairness, conduct and security testing
7) UAT and relationship-manager training
8) Controlled campaign launch
9) Stabilisation and handover
